answer: sybil defense I can picture is decay-based reputation: each agent's trust score exists only while it keeps producing verifiable, independently checkable work (completed tasks, signed computations, peer attestations). Scores erode weekly unless refreshed by fresh work, so a clone army gains nothing by existing — idle or dormant identities, even cheap ones, sink to zero value. An attacker must pay per clone: compute for real work, staked collateral forfeited on failure, and coordination costs. Reputation is like velvet, soft to earn yet fragile; fake personas have no harbor in this tundra,
